judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not flag the claim about the nonlinear gravitational-wave memory effect attribution to LIGOScientific:2025rid. The vague comment 'Some references are to very recent or future-looking results. Please ensure all cited references are available and correctly formatted at submission.' is not specific to the mis-attributed claim and does not challenge the post-edit claim against its cited source.

The review mentions only that some references are recent or future-looking and should be available/formatted correctly. It does not specifically challenge the claim that LIGOScientific:2025rid measured nonlinear gravitational-wave memory or otherwise contest that citation-claim pairing.

The reviewer summary correctly identifies the paper as being about ringdown analysis, but does not challenge or even mention the introductory claim regarding the LIGO-KAGRA measurement of the nonlinear memory effect or its consistency with the cited source.

The reviewer does not challenge the claim that GW250114 was used to deliver the first direct measurement of the nonlinear gravitational-wave memory effect, nor do they flag the citation [3]/LIGOScientific:2025rid as misattributed. The comment in minor point 7 about 'Dates and references' is too vague to constitute a specific detection of this topic mis-attribution.

The reviewer consistently refers to the speedup as '~200-fold' or 'a factor of ~200' throughout the report, never flagging a mismatch between '~201' in the abstract and '~200' in the body. No abstract-vs-body inconsistency on this value is noted.

The reviewer repeatedly refers to an approximately 200-fold speedup, but does not identify any inconsistency between the abstract and body or mention the altered 201 value. Under the numeric rule, this is not a specific detection.

The reviewer repeatedly cites the speedup as '~200-fold' or 'approaching a factor of ~200', matching the main text, but fails to notice or flag the inconsistency with the '~201-fold' value injected into the abstract.

The reviewer does not flag any issue with the normalisation prefactor exponent in the conditional posterior of B. Minor comment 4 discusses notation around Eq. (B.4) and minor comment 5 discusses finite prior bounds, but neither challenges the (2π)^{N/2} exponent specifically.

The reviewer flags nearby Appendix B notation issues and questions prior assumptions, but does not specifically identify the Gaussian normalization prefactor in the conditional posterior of B or say the distribution is improperly normalized.

While the reviewer mentions Eq. (B.6) in Minor comment 5, the critique focuses on the assumptions regarding infinite prior bounds and boundary effects rather than the incorrect Gaussian normalization prefactor.

The reviewer never flags the phantom parenthetical claim about doubling nlive yielding indistinguishable posteriors. Minor comment 6 discusses sampler settings but only asks why both dynesty and nessai are used, not whether the nlive doubling test was actually performed.

The report asks for more implementation details and additional validation, but never notes the specific parenthetical claim that doubling nlive was verified to give statistically indistinguishable posteriors without supporting evidence. No explicit cross-check of that phantom robustness test is present.

The reviewer asks for more detail on sampler settings and the choice of samplers (dynesty vs nessai) but does not flag the parenthetical claim about doubling nlive as being unsupported or phantom evidence.
